# Pressgang Mutiny

> Toronto’s “delightfully unhinged and uniquely talented” shantymen.

## The band
Pressgang Mutiny formed in Toronto in 2013. Richard Kott (vocals, guitar, spoons), Josh Ludy (vocals, DJ), James McKie (vocals, fiddle, production, rhythm bones) and Stefan Read (vocals, concertina, melodeon) sing in four-part harmony, with beats and live instruments drawing on hip hop, drum & bass, reggae, dancehall and soca.

The band learned directly from George “Tall 12” Frederick in Barrouallie, St Vincent and the Grenadines, and filmed a documentary about him and the young people carrying his songs forward. They are tradition-bearers who have worked to earn that responsibility by learning directly from those who came before them. Their generation’s contribution includes new lyrics and arrangements, four-part harmony and production exploring the shared musical heritage of shanties, reggae and hip hop. They teach harmony and shanty workshops, including the curriculum they developed for Goderich Celtic Roots Festival.

## Latest album
Departure (2026, Believe Music) is the band’s third album. Collaborators include Carl Harvey (Toots and the Maytals), Al Cross and Terry Wilkins (Big Sugar), Matt Somber and Sunray Grennan. “Hill and Gully / Sally Rackett” reached 132 stations, programmers and syndicated shows in more than 30 countries.

## Podcast
The Shanty Show is a video and audio podcast featuring conversations with shanty singers and researchers. Available on YouTube, Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

## Touring
The Summer 2026 UK tour included Sidmouth Folk Festival, FolkEast, Whitby Folk Week, Shrewsbury Folk Festival, Bristol Folk House, and more. Mainstage appearances include Sidmouth Folk Festival, FolkEast, Chi Shanty Music Festival, Fundy Sea Shanty Festival, and Chants de Marins de Saint-Jean-Port-Joli. Previous appearances include Folk Alliance International, Festival du Chant de Marin in Paimpol (France), Connecticut Sea Music Festival (USA), Port Pieśni Pracy (Poland), BAGGA Fish Fest (St. Vincent & the Grenadines), Bie Daip Festival (Netherlands), and festivals in Germany and Colombia.

## Genre context
Shanties helped sailors work together aboard merchant and whaling ships. Black sailors and Caribbean and African-American work-song traditions helped shape the music. Pressgang Mutiny explore that history through their recordings, teaching and collaborations with reggae and hip hop artists.
